title: Setting up {{project}}
description: The major calls almost every new project or plugin setup needs: visibility, licence, where outputs go and how far the agent may go alone.
context: Setup questions for {{project}}, from the askwright project-setup template.

questions.title: Public or private
questions.question: Should {{project}} live in a public or a private repository?
questions.why: Decides where it is pushed, whether CI runs on hosted runners and what may be committed.
questions.background: A new project needs a home before the first push. Public repositories get free hosted CI and can be shared; private ones keep work and assets out of sight but need self-hosted runners for CI.

options.label: Public repository
options.consequence: Nothing private, licensed or personal is committed.

options.label: Private repository
options.consequence: CI runs on a self-hosted runner.

options.label: No remote yet, keep it local

guess.why: Safer default until it is ready to share.

questions.title: Licence
questions.question: Which licence should {{project}} carry?
questions.why: Decides what others may do with the code and which assets can be included.
questions.background: Every shared repository needs a licence file; without one nobody may legally reuse it. MIT is short and permissive; Apache-2.0 adds a patent grant; all rights reserved keeps everything.

guess.why: The usual choice for small tools and plugins.

questions.title: Where outputs go
questions.question: Which folder should generated outputs (renders, builds, exports) be written to?
questions.why: Keeps large generated files out of the repository and in one place you can find.
questions.background: Setup scripts write outputs somewhere by default. A folder outside the repository keeps commits small; a folder inside it (git-ignored) keeps everything together.

guess.text: an out/ folder inside the project, git-ignored
guess.why: Easy to find and never committed.

questions.title: How far to go alone
questions.question: How far may the agent go on {{project}} without asking?
questions.why: Sets when work stops for your review and when it carries on.
questions.background: Agents can stop at a pull request, merge their own once checks pass, or also tag releases. Publishing to a package registry always waits for an explicit go-ahead.

options.label: Merge own pull requests once checks pass
Merge and cut GitHub releases too

guess.why: Matches how most of your own repositories run.
